title: Synthesis and Physico-Chemical Analysis of Dextran from Maltodextrin via pH Controlled Fermentation by Gluconobacter oxydans
content: Dextran is an exopolysaccharide (EPS) with multifunctional applications in food and pharmaceutical industries, primarily synthesized from Leuconostoc mesenteroides. Dextran can be produced from dextrin through Gluconobacter oxydans fermentation, utilizing its dextran dextrinase activity. This study examines how jar fermentor conditions impact the growth and enzyme activity of G. oxydans, with a focus on pH effects on dextran synthesis via bioconversion (without pH control, pH 4.5, and pH 5.0; Jp-UC, Jp-4.5, and Jp-5.0). After 72 hours, cell density (O.D. at 600 nm) was 7.2 for Jp-4.5, 6.5 for Jp-5.0, and 3.7 for Jp-UC. Flow property analysis, indicating EPS production, showed that Jp-4.5 had the highest viscosity (30.99 mPa·s). 1H-NMR analysis confirmed the formation of α-1,6 glycosidic bonds in bioconversion products, with bond ratios ranging from ~1:0.17 to ~1:2.84. The molecular weights distribution varied from 1.3 × 10³ Da to 5.1 × 10⁴ Da depending on pH. The hydrolysis rates to glucose differed with pH, with the slowest rate at pH 4.5 (53.96%). These results suggest that the production of dextran by G. oxydans is significantly influenced by pH conditions. This dextran could function as a slowly digestible carbohydrate, aiding in postprandial glycemic regulation and mitigating chronic metabolic diseases like diabetes.
